args.message:
fix(money): use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212

round_money was quantizing with ROUND_HALF_UP, so half-cent values were
always rounded away from zero. FIN-212 requires banker's rounding, which
rounds ties to the nearest even cent (2.675 -> 2.68, 2.665 -> 2.66).

files.content:
# Changelog

## Unreleased

- Fix `round_money` to use banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`) as required by FIN-212.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: fix(money): implement banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary

`src/money.py` documented banker's rounding but actually quantized with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, causing the nightly build to fail on `tests/test_money.py`.

This changes `round_money` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` as required by FIN-212:

- `Decimal("2.675")` -> `2.68`
- `Decimal("2.665")` -> `2.66` (tie rounds to the even cent)

## Changes

- `src/money.py`: `ROUND_HALF_UP` -> `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (import + quantize call).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: note under Unreleased.

## Testing

CI on this branch passed (run `ci-0001`, sha `ed19cae5f5`), including `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even`.

## Risk

Low — behavior change only affects exact half-cent ties, which is the intended FIN-212 behavior. Any downstream reconciliation reports that assumed half-up tie-breaking will shift by one cent on ties.

5. **Re-ran CI** (`ci-0002`, sha `b12e279422`) — passed, including `test_half_even`.
6. **Opened PR #101** against `main` with alex requested as reviewer: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

**Not done, deliberately:** I did not merge. Merging to `main` requires code-owner approval, and alex's review is the approval path — that's now pending on your side.

**Worth flagging:** the behavior change only affects exact half-cent ties, but any downstream reconciliation or reporting code that assumed half-up tie-breaking will shift by one cent on those values. The PR body notes this; worth a sanity check from whoever owns reconciliation before it lands.
